answer.sourceLine: From her Autobiographical Notes, printed with her biography Pierre Curie (New York: Macmillan, 1923). The original reads “I have been frequently questioned, especially by women, how I could reconcile family life with a scientific career. Well, it has not been easy; it required a great deal of decision and of self-sacrifice.” The popular version slightly rewords the first sentence and cuts off the second.

source.excerpt: But of course the care of my children’s education was only a part of my duties, my professional occupations taking most of my time. I have been frequently questioned, especially by women, how I could reconcile family life with a scientific career. Well, it has not been easy; it required a great deal of decision and of self-sacrifice. However, the family bond has been preserved between me and my now grown-up daughters, and life is made brighter by the mutual affection and understanding in our home, where I could not suffer a harsh word or selfish behavior.

author.name: Marie Curie
author.heading: About Marie Curie
author.bio: Marie Curie (born Maria Skłodowska) was the pioneer of radioactivity research who won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1903) and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1911). After her husband Pierre died, she wrote his biography. Its English edition, Pierre Curie (1923), also carried her own short Autobiographical Notes, which she says she wrote because “my American friends” asked for the story of her life.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line comes from the short autobiography Marie Curie added to the English edition of her book about her husband. She opens it: “I have been asked by my American friends to write the story of my life.” In the same opening paragraph she calls her life one “which has not been easy on the whole.” The family-life passage comes in Chapter II, just after she describes arranging her daughters’ schooling and their physical education.

The full passage is less tidy than the meme version. She admits that combining children and a laboratory “required a great deal of decision and of self-sacrifice,” and then says the family bond with her “now grown-up daughters” had been preserved.
